mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflation risk, which compresses real growth and raises uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls by more than 10% month-on-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows positive and increasing month-on-month changes for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS shows two consecutive months of accelerating growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month averages indicates strengthening aggregate demand, which lifts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.
